evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: ensuring accurate settlement between our customers, external financial institutions, and Rippling for every transaction
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Responsibilities center on reconciliation accuracy, regulatory/compliance reporting, and audit support with no velocity/speed language present.
evidence.domain_risk: critical for Rippling's finances... regulatory & compliance reporting, and Internal and External Audit reporting
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: The role directly touches financial reporting, reconciliation, and regulatory/audit compliance for payments data, a default-high fintech domain reinforced by explicit compliance language.
evidence.collaboration_width: Accounting; Finance; Biz Ops; Payments; Product; Compliance; Treasury; engineering; financial partnerships
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: The team already exists with a defined charter (Payments Data & Analytics) and is scaling, not being built from zero, but is not described as large/established at scale either.
evidence.jd_authorship: Monitor payment flows between systems, banks, processors, and inter-company accounts, perform daily account reconciliations, and follow up on any discrepancies.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Responsibilities give precise, concrete day-to-day tasks (reconciliations, payment flow monitoring, month-end close support) that a reader can clearly picture.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: You will empower the Accounting, Finance, Biz Ops, Payments, and Product teams
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The role's primary audience is Finance/Accounting functions (reconciliation, month-end close, audit/regulatory reporting), placing it squarely in finance orientation despite some product/eng collaboration.
evidence.autonomy_level: Collaborate with key stakeholders... to understand business requirements and develop scalable solutions
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The role both builds foundational reconciliation/reporting infrastructure (strategic) and responds to and delivers against stakeholder requirements (execution), placing it as mixed.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: No mention of AI tools, AI-assisted coding, or AI-consuming data infrastructure anywhere in the JD.
evidence.testing_framing: No testing or data quality framework language present.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: The JD discusses reconciliation and accuracy but never references data testing, data contracts, or quality frameworks as a named practice or tool.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: essential for the correct functioning of product systems... regulatory & compliance reporting, and Internal and External Audit reporting
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: High loss-aversion framing dominates: the role summary itself frames the job around ensuring accurate settlement and audit/regulatory reporting, i.e., preventing bad financial data from reaching stakeholders or auditors.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: become a foundational member of the Payments Analytics team
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: The role is foundational/building-out (reconciliation automation, internal tool development) within an already-existing but expanding team, giving a mixed greenfield/fix-scale signal.
evidence.loss_aversion: "React swiftly to emerging issues, summarize facts, and provide recommendations for the timely resolution of critical financial matters" — reflects fear of financial/reconciliation failures reaching stakeholders.
